rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-2: platforms comply with the registry rule (display numbers, remove listings on notice), so open on-platform lets stop.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-4: some guests keep wanting whole units in Saltmere enough to book them directly.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-3: for some units complaints are unlikely, so the expected fine is below the gain from breach (enforcement is on complaint only).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-19: neighbors file complaints about unlawful lets in meaningful numbers and some lead to fines.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-5, inverted: A-5 puts at 0.85 that most non-primary units can be let on 12-month leases, so the statement that the hosts cannot replace short lets with other uses for most of their business is 0.15.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-8: hotels are a substitute for whole units for some guests.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-14: hosts, platforms, hotels and neighborhood associations can organize at a cost below their stake.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-10: Elsdon is near enough (12 km from Harbor) for some guests.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-38: some owners reshape short stays into nominal 30-night contracts, or claim primary residence on documents they can change at low cost.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-15: guests can book summer stays earlier than they otherwise would.

No matching assumption in WE-044; judged from the text: the $250 fee (against $150 under the old registration) and proof of residence are a fixed cost per host that goes beyond what some hosts who let only a few nights already meet.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-2: platforms display registration numbers and remove listings on notice, so lets without a number largely stop.

No matching assumption in WE-044; judged from the text: about 550 primary-residence units are let, about 65% of hosts already register under the old rule, and registration is the only way to keep letting short.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-22: hosts listing on more than one platform can exceed 90 nights without the per-platform reports revealing it (and list under another unit's number).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-8: hotels are a substitute for whole units for some guests.
No matching assumption in WE-044; judged from the text: registration requires only proof of residence and a fee; it tests nothing about the stay that guests value and cannot judge.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-14: hosts, platforms, hotels and neighborhood associations can organize at a cost below their stake.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-044 (illustrative figures), A-20: the $520,000 for the Registry Unit is new general-fund money.
